title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
summary: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer k, provide the k-th smallest value of all node values in the tree, where k is 1-indexed.
statement: Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer k, provide the k-th smallest value of all node values in the tree, where k is 1-indexed.
constraints: 1 <= k <= node count <= 10,000. Node values are in [0, 10,000].
The input is a binary search tree. k is one-indexed.

hints: Inorder traversal of a BST visits values in increasing order.
Use a stack to reach the next smallest unvisited node without sorting all values.
Push a left spine, pop and decrement k, return at zero, then traverse the popped node's right subtree.
An explicit stack also handles highly skewed trees without Python recursion-depth errors.
editorial: Push the root's entire left spine. The next popped node is the smallest unvisited value. Decrement the remaining rank and return its value when the rank reaches zero. Otherwise visit its right subtree by pushing that subtree's left spine. Each visited node is processed once, with O(h) stack entries and O(h+k) time before the kth result.
